answer: Each identity claims one grove plot, locks 70 credits as bond, and pays a garden toll. Tolls rise per grove: first claim 40; k-th claim on the same grove 20k plus 20, so tenth copy 220, thousandth 20020. A garden keeper signs only after inspecting the grove at the pulse audit, binding grove, keeper, and audit in the receipt hash. Anyone can recompute it and check each hash once. A ring copying one grove to 1000 identities pays 10030000. A rented garden receipt fails: its hash is already claimed, and the bond burns. An honest identity claims one grove and pays 40 once.
